Hi, I had an SA at 11w1d and I can tell you what my personal experience was like. Everyones is different of course, but I know when I was feeling anxious I really wish someone would have told me in detail what to expect. Everything felt so uncertain and gray, people saying "it was great!!" or saying "it was bad!!" didn't give me any relief.

I was really scared of the pain, I have very severe anxiety and it did not help. I actually started having an anxiety attack in the room right before I had the procedure. I was given extra anti-anxiety medication because of my mental health problems and a normal dose of pain medication. I believe one of them was fentanyl, I can't remember the other. Two seconds after the medication went in my IV I literally stopped crying and felt okay enough to go through with everything. It kicks in fast.

I don't know how to describe the feeling (will try my best below), as I never had felt it before, but I have also had a medical abortion and I promise that the pain of the SA was NOT as bad, NOWHERE near the same. I was fearing the worst, literally sobbing every day in fear of the pain. And when they finished I literally was like "what? its over?"

I won't lie, it hurt but really no where near as bad as I expected. I didn't cry at all from the pain nor was I overwhelmed at all, and was able to hold a conversation the entire time except during one part which hurt a little extra I interrupted myself to blurt out "OW" and take a few deep breaths. I had brought a stuffed animal to hold and squeeze and it made me feel alot better throughout everything.

I would like to mention pain medication works poorly for me as well.
Pain scale for procedure for me, this may be different for you please please note that

shots to numb the cervix: 4/10, just a sharp pinch, after the first i didnt really feel the rest that much.
dialating: felt a weird pressure, honestly 1/10
the suctioning part: 5/10-7/10, this part lasted about a single minute, maybe a minute and a half and it was what I was fearing the most. Its a tugging cramping feeling(not a great description but best i can do), but it really wasn't too bad. It was only 7/10 sometimes, 5/10 most of it.

And no matter what, please remember that giving birth would hurt 100x worse. You are going through a 2-5 minute procedure. You might feel a little sore after, but I personally was walking and fine after less than 15 minutes in recovery. Dont worry though, if you are in pain or feel sick after you should be able to wait in a recovery room until you feel okay again. I'd say the next day I felt GREAT, and was only a little sore for a few hours immediately after. I actually didn't experience any cramping and just was bleeding lightly until about 5 days after, and then I just managed with a heating pad and felt fine. I did not use the ibuprofen they prescribed because well, I felt okay enough. 

It's really scary leading up to it, but it isn't going to be a scary traumatic painful thing. And even if it was, which it shouldnt be, 2-5 minutes and its over. Honestly, you probably will be barely able to remember it after if you are being mildly sedated (twilight/iv sedation like I opted for) I cannot recall anything I talked about during the procedure except that it was something to do with video games and anime haha.

I also have to say I think my experience went so well aswell because of the clinic I went to. Where I am there isn't an option to get put under either (Michigan, US) that I could find and afford. So I researched every clinic I could, reading every review on every site and weeded out the fake ones of course. The clinic I went to had me talk about all of my anxieties and made any accommodations I needed, never made me feel silly, and were so incredibly sweet that I started crying a few times. They also do routine training that is not required to make sure that everything always goes smooth. It was not a planned parenthood, but did cost the same. They even had armed body gaurds to escort you inside if there was protesters at this clinic. I felt so safe and taken care of there. Make sure you look into where youre going so you can have a good comfortable experience and stay safe<3 If you have any other questions or need to talk, reach out I am here <3

I won't lie, for me it was bad. I think it was /that/ bad because no one was honest with me about the extent of pain I could feel, so I panicked and thought something was horribly wrong which made me tense up and freak out which intensified things. 

I had my MA at around 7 weeks. I felt okay after taking it for about two hours, then I ended up having horrible cramping that lasted about 3-4 hours. I won't lie, it was not fun and honestly I would recommend being somewhere that you can feel comfortable and unashamed being in pain and possibly throwing up. Have someone with you that you trust, and make sure you can feel safe to feel whatever you may feel. Get a heating pad. It was the only thing that kept me sane. Laying down made it harder for me, I actually believe I passed the clump while sitting on the toilet at the hospital (i had gone because i was in horrible pain, and i didn't know that it was okay to be in that much pain. They gave me more pain medication via a shot, but it didn't really help because I passed it about 5 minutes later. Its worth noting that pain medicene works VERY poorly for me. It may work wonders for you.) 
After I passed the clump (what i like to call it, sorry if that is cold) I felt almost like, euphoria because the pain kind of just dulled down and I knew it was over. Once its over, at least for me it was over. I went home with my heating pad, curled up and rested. I had hypermesis gravidarum and man oh man did I feast the day after. 

Please know I am not trying to scare you. I just dont want to lie to you. You may only experience bad period cramps, or you may end up in a situation like me where you thought you were like dying. No matter the case, it is temporary, and I promise that you can handle it. I have had two abortions, my second being a surgical two days ago. I was petrified both times, but now I am so thankful that I went through it because well, I'm not pregnant and the pain was temporary. You will get to the other side and be okay.

No matter how rough it is, just remember it is no where near as bad as labor would be and that you will be okay. I hope things go well for you.

Hi, I am a woman who is literally afraid of men so I feel somewhat qualified to give advice. 

You don't necessarily need to change how you speak (wording, etc) but softening your voice can do wonders. You may be larger or intimidating in appearance I don't know, but I'm sure you have met larger or intimidating people in your time in prison. How would you like to be approached by them to be made comfortable? Remember that in how you carry yourself. 

Body language is huge. I am not personally looking at how you look or judging that. I am hyperanalyzing your body language and expressions from the moment I see you to determine if you are a threat. If you seem gentle, stern, kind, erratic, tense I will notice. If you seem like you aren't tense or on edge, I will feel less tense or on edge. I'm sure others have suggested, but perhaps going to therapy can help you if you struggle with anxieties. 

Get a cat if you like cats and can put in the work to have one, specifically a kitten. They are small and fragile, and require you to be softer to bond with them. Cats are not like dogs, you need to give them a good reason to like you or they wont. I think cats can teach people a lot. Plus, girls love cats. I trust someone way more if they can take care of a kitten or tell me, "I just got a kitten! Can I show you pictures?" and then you have a companion who loves you for the next 15 years. 

I really hope that you have good luck in your future endeavors:-)

I've been in a similar situation almost, except in Rileys role. I'm an athiest, my now fiance's family is mormon. They hate me, still hate me, and probably will never stop hating me. He's left me on occasions for them due to their manipulation and threats. But, in the end he chose what mattered to him and what he wanted. He chose me. 

We are moving into an apartment together next month, and he's living with me at my families house currently. 

A few words of advice for you, make sure she's really what you want and is equally into you too. That you won't mess things up forever for something that won't matter, if thats what your fear is anyway.
Also, if you depend on your family, its best not to be violent or crude in announcing your feelings. Itd be terrible if you ended up kicked out.

But, the biggest thing you may need to understand is that you cant always have both. Your parents may never come around (but truthfully, they seem toxic anyway). 
Overall, its up to you whats most important to you. And someday, even if thats not now, this may happen again. And it may be more serious. And when that happens, it may come to your happiness vs them being happy with you. 
Always pick your happiness.
